results.title: US experts join Ghana’s fight against mercury pollution in rivers
results.content: A team of United States scientists visited Ghana to support efforts to tackle mercury pollution linked to illegal small-scale gold mining and strengthen freshwater protection.

results.title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns
results.content: Nvidia's market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect.

results.title: Court restrains CLOGSAG’s 15th Quadrennial National Congress
results.content: The High Court in Accra has granted an interim injunction restraining the Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) from holding its 15th Quadrennial National Congress scheduled for November 23 to 25, 2026.

results.title: Presidency orders compulsory retirement, handover for CEOs aged 60
results.content: The Presidency has directed ministers of state to enforce the constitutional retirement age of 60 for chief executives of public institutions and state-owned enterprises under their supervision. The directive requires affected executives who have attained the compulsory retirement age and do not have valid post-retirement contracts to prepare their handover notes and leave office without […]

results.title: Presidency orders state CEOs who have reached retirement limits to vacate office
results.content: Chief Executives of public institutions and state-owned organisations who have exceeded the constitutional retirement limits have been directed to hand over and vacate office, following a new instruction from the Office of the President. The directive requires all Ministers of State to ensure that CEOs under their respective oversight comply with Article 199 of the 1992 Constitution, which sets the compulsory retirement age for public officers at 60, subject to specified exceptions and re-engagement arrangements.

results.title: Ghana Bauxite Company commits to opening Awaso to commercial activity
results.content: The Ghana Bauxite Company Limited says it is deliberately using its expanding operations at Awaso to open the catchment communities to wider commercial activity.

results.title: US Exchange Alumni Summit: Past fellow struggle to access post-fellowship grants, limiting knowledge-transfer applications
results.content: A 2019 Mandela Washington Fellow, Dr Joel Afi Duah, says it is becoming increasingly difficult for beneficiaries of development programs in the United States of America to access post-fellowship grants following donor cuts in the US.

results.title: Early BECE ban ineffective without student tracking system – Africa Education Watch
results.content: The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, says the repeated ban on exceptionally gifted pupils sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) ahead of schedule will remain ineffective without a system to track students across schools.

results.title: Pharmaceutical hub in Kwenyako targets 20,000 jobs; Ghana eyes 80% essential medicine production locally – Mahama
results.content: President John Mahama says the government plans to establish a pharmaceutical and biomanufacturing hub in Kwenyako in the Asuogyaman District in the Eastern Region as part of efforts to boost local production of medicines and vaccines and create approximately 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.

results.title: Mason arrested over death of 9-year-old son at Kwahu Kotoso
results.content: A 32-year-old mason has been arrested by the Kwahu Tafo Police in connection with the death of his nine-year-old son at Kwahu Kotoso in the Eastern Region.

results.title: One injured as fire destroys brothel at Asankragua Market
results.content: One person has sustained a dislocated right shoulder after a fire destroyed a wooden structure used as a brothel at Asankragua Market in the Western Region.

results.title: Church elder killed, 4 injured in motorbike-tricycle crash at Assin Kokompe
results.content: A 45-year-old church elder has died, while four others have sustained injuries, following a head-on collision between a motorbike and a motorised tricycle at Assin Kokompe in the Assin North District of the Central Region.

results.title: Upper West bids farewell to Regional Police Commander, enskins him as Chelihipuorinye Naa
results.content: There was a time when fear gripped almost every household in Wa. Violent crime, armed robbery and localised tensions threatened the very fabric of society. Communities lived in fear and uncertainty.

results.title: KATH Biostatistics Unit wants health information professionals represented in hospital management
results.content: The Biostatistics Unit of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) has called for greater recognition of health information professionals in hospital management, emphasising the importance of reliable data in improving healthcare delivery and patient outcomes.

results.title: Tweneboah Koduah SHS old students donate over 50 beds, raise funds for school development
results.content: Old students of Tweneboah Koduah Senior High School have donated over 50 student beds and raised funds to support infrastructure development at the school as part of efforts to improve teaching and learning conditions.

results.title: Gifted children should not be punished for advancing faster – Offinso North MP
results.content: Member of Parliament for Offinso North and member of Parliament’s Education Committee, Fred Kyei Asamoah, has challenged the government to provide evidence to justify its decision to prevent exceptionally gifted children from writing the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) ahead of schedule.

results.title: Allowing children to write BECE early defeats 9-year basic education policy – Nortsu-Kotoe
results.content: Chairman of Parliament’s Education Committee, Peter Kwasi Nortsu-Kotoe, has defended the requirement for candidates to complete nine years of basic education before writing the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE), arguing that allowing pupils to sit the examination earlier undermines the country’s education policy.

results.title: Fire Service records 53 fires, 8 deaths, and 10 injuries from September 1 to November 2
results.content: Over two months, Ghana recorded 53 major fires. Eight people died and 10 were injured. The figures come from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) report covering September 1 to November 2, 2026.

results.title: KsTU records 40% female enrolment in push for gender parity in TVET
results.content: Kumasi Technical University (KsTU) has recorded a 40 per cent female enrolment for the 2026/2027 academic year, as the institution intensifies efforts to promote gender participation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

results.title: GES postpones opening of teacher recruitment portal to November 25
results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has postponed the opening of its teacher recruitment portal, which was expected to become operational on Monday, November 23, to Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

results.title: President Mahama visits Chris Hesse, recounts efforts to save Ghana’s historical archives
results.content: President John Mahama has visited veteran filmmaker and photographer Chris Hesse, who served as the personal cinematographer to Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, recounting how they worked together to save the country's historical film archives from deterioration and possible destruction. The President said their efforts began when he was Deputy Minister of Communications, after Mr Hesse took him to the Information Services Department to see old film reels that were deteriorating and had become mouldy. He said they made efforts to retrieve some of the films but could not save others because of the extent of the damage. President Mahama explained that Mr Hesse later informed him that well-preserved copies of the films were being kept at a Rank Xerox laboratory in London. results.title: Foreigners taking over Ghana’s retail market a worrying trend – Kumasi Mayor
results.content: Kumasi Mayor Richard Ofori-Agyemang Boadi has described the growing involvement of foreign nationals in Ghana’s retail trade as a worrying trend, warning that it could undermine the interests of local businesses if urgent action is not taken.

results.title: Cause of fire at Northern Regional Coordinating Council yet to be established – GNFS
results.content: The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) says investigations are underway to establish the cause of a fire that destroyed parts of the Northern Regional Coordinating Council building in Tamale.

results.title: Regular JHS pupils must complete three years before BECE – WAEC
results.content: Regular Junior High School (JHS) pupils must complete all three years of the programme before sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE), the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) has reiterated. The Council says students enrolled in regular schools are not eligible to register for the private BECE, popularly known as NOVDEC, which is reserved for individuals who are not in regular school and candidates seeking to improve grades obtained in previous examinations. Speaking on JoyNews' Top Story on Monday, November 23, 2026, WAEC's Deputy Director of Public Affairs, Lilian Frimpong, said it was illegal for regular JHS students to register for the private examination. results.title: UniMAC graduates 1,414 as university targets AI-driven creative economy
results.content: The University of Media, Arts and Communication (UniMAC) has graduated 1,414 students, recording a 57.6 per cent increase over its 2025 graduating class

results.title: Tyson Fury diagnosed with schizophrenia
results.content: Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

results.title: Hiplife Trinity reunion highlights need to bring Ghana’s music legends back
results.content: The reunion of Reggie Rockstone, Obrafour and Tic Tac has reignited calls for regular concerts celebrating Ghana’s music legends

results.title: Greater Accra Regional Minister urges public to report theft of street lights
results.content: Greater Accra Regional Minister Linda Ocloo has urged residents to report incidents of street light theft in their communities, describing the practice as a major challenge to efforts to improve public lighting across the region.

results.title: USA, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to co-host inaugural 48-team 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup
results.content: FIFA’s Member Associations (MAs) convened virtually at an Extraordinary Congress today and appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as the hosts of the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031, the first edition to feature 48 teams and across four MAs, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed to stage FIFA’s flagship women’s competition in 2035.

results.title: National security restores calm at Suame Magazine as GUTA backs closure of foreigners’ shops
results.content: The Ghana Union of Traders Associations (GUTA) in the Ashanti Region has thrown its support behind the closure of some shops owned by foreign nationals at Suame Magazine in Kumasi.
